findings.title: Controller declares linear acceleration limit 1.20x the downstream smoother limit
findings.summary: Controller `ax_max` = 3.0 m/s^2 (controller_server.ros__parameters.FollowPath.ax_max); downstream velocity_smoother `max_accel[0]` = 2.5 m/s^2 (velocity_smoother.ros__parameters.max_accel[0]). The controller's figure exceeds the smoother's by 1.20x, and the smoother is what the base actually receives.
findings.details: The controller rolls out and validates candidate trajectories against its own figure. Because the smoother caps what actually reaches the base, a trajectory accepted as feasible or collision-free under the controller's figure may not be achievable in execution. This leans in the unsafe direction. Whether this is a defect depends on intent, which is not recorded in the configuration: a generically-tuned controller paired with a platform-tuned smoother can produce this legitimately. EAL reports both values and the direction; the judgement is yours.
findings.suggested_fix: Reconcile the two declarations: either raise `velocity_smoother.max_accel[0]` to 3.0, or lower `ax_max` to 2.5, whichever matches the platform's real capability.

unchecked_hazards.statement: Hazard classes EAL does not check. A review that reports no findings says nothing about any of these. Measured by the adversarial evaluation in eval/, not asserted.

classes.title: Contradictory definitions in unexamined locations
classes.detail: Duplicate keys in one mapping are detected. A second controller plugin block with contradictory limits is not: the importer resolves the first plugin entry and never inspects alternatives.

classes.title: Physically implausible declared capability
classes.detail: EAL checks that declarations agree with each other, never that any of them is achievable. A platform declaring roughly ten g of braking, or zero actuation delay alongside a half-second control loop, is accepted without comment.

classes.title: Slower control or perception loop
classes.detail: Control frequency, costmap update rate, transform tolerance, and source timeouts are extracted as timing parameters but are never related to the speed the robot is permitted to travel. Sensor and actuator latency are absent from Nav2 configuration entirely and are not modelled at all.

classes.title: Speed raised within an internally consistent configuration
classes.detail: EAL compares the controller's declared limits against the downstream clamp. A speed increase applied to both keeps them in agreement and is not examined. Nothing relates speed to braking capability, sensor range, or stopping distance.

classes.title: Weakened braking within an internally consistent configuration
classes.detail: As with speed: a deceleration limit lowered on both the controller and the smoother keeps them in agreement. Stopping distance is not modelled, so a coherent reduction in braking authority is invisible.

classes.title: An entire configuration section absent
classes.detail: A missing individual limit is reported as an incomplete comparison. A missing whole section, such as no velocity smoother at all, is treated as the check being inapplicable rather than unknown. That judgement is arguable and is recorded here so it stays visible.

classes.title: Reduced sensing range or clearance margin
classes.detail: Sensor marking range, raytrace range, and inflation radius are extracted but no check consumes them. A robot configured so that it cannot detect an obstacle in time to stop produces no finding.

classes.title: Unit errors applied consistently
classes.detail: A unit conversion mistake made on both sides of a comparison is arithmetically coherent. EAL has no notion of a plausible magnitude for a physical quantity, so it cannot tell metres from feet or radians from degrees.
